newsitem.title: UK: Merrill Lynch sees six global 'superbanks' ahead.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch sees six global 'superbanks' ahead.

text.p: A monopoly of six global 'superbanks' is likely to result from the continuing amalgamation of banks, insurance and securities firms according to Merrill Lynch.

Paul Roy, managing director Europe, Middle East, and South Africa at the U.S. investment bank, said this week that further mergers and aquisitions were inevitable, and were likely to be cross-functional.

"The overall requirements for globalisation have become so daunting and rigorous that no more than a half-dozen or so full-service firms will occupy leadership positions as truly global players," Roy told a London conference on globalisation of the securities markets.
"There will be some winners, some also-rans and a goodly number of losers."

He told Reuters in an interview after his speech that Merrill would be at the forefront of such a group of 'superbanks', as it had long predicted and been preparing for continued consolidation across the sector.
"We are in a race of leadership and the lines will continue to blur," he said.
Deals in the financial sector have become increasingly cross-functional, as banks realise they must offer securities products in order to survive in a client-driven evolution of financial services.

This has seen barriers lifted and securities markets become Recently announced deals included a merger between Bankers Trust and securities firm Alex Brown, and Morgan Stanley's merger with Dean Whitter.
Roy said in a few years more than 50 percent of the top dozen securities firms were likely to be owned by banks or other financial intermediaries.
And he added that the move towards global superbanks would necessitate changes to regulation.
"As demonstrated by the Barings and Daiwa incidents, the world's financial supervisors...will be continually challenged in their efforts to ensure a stable financial system," he said.
